easy.q: When President Eyring was a little boy, he asked his mother why life is so hard. What did she tell him?
options: Life gets easier when you grow up
Life is a test
Life is hard only for some people
easy.why: His mother smiled and said firmly, “Hal, of course it’s hard. It’s supposed to be. Life is a test.”

easy.q: President Eyring spoke about a hymn the choir had just sung. What did he say about the promises in that hymn?
options: The promises are true
The promises were only for long ago
The promises are only for a few people
easy.why: He said, “My message today is that the promises in that hymn are true.” They can guide and comfort each of us in our trials.

easy.q: What was the only picture President Eyring’s mother placed on her bedroom wall?
options: A picture of her family
A picture of the temple
A picture of the Savior
easy.why: The only picture on her wall was of the Savior, and it hung where she could see it as she lay in her bed.

easy.q: What did President Eyring’s father do for the nurses who had helped his wife in the hospital?
options: He mailed each of them a card
He thanked each one and shook hands
He brought each of them flowers
easy.why: His father walked through the hospital ward to thank and shake the hand of every nurse who had helped her.

easy.q: According to President Eyring, what simple thing can help a discouraged missionary feel that the Lord is watching over them?
options: A kind word or a warm smile
A day off from their work
A box of treats from home
easy.why: He taught that kindness, “even for a few seconds, or simply a warm smile,” can strengthen a missionary’s faith that the Lord is watching over them.

medium.q: What did President Eyring say is important to realize about the promise “Fear not, I am with thee”?
options: It applies mainly to times of sickness
It is fulfilled only after this life
It is not a promise that challenges will be removed
It depends on our never feeling afraid
medium.why: He said, “It is important to realize that the promise is not for the removal of challenges.” The Lord promises to be with us and strengthen us in them.

medium.q: Why, according to President Eyring, does a loving and all-powerful God allow our mortal test to be so hard?
options: We must grow in spiritual cleanliness and stature to live with Him
Hard things come by chance and carry no lasting purpose
He wants us to learn to manage without help from others
Trials are mostly the result of what others choose to do
medium.why: President Eyring taught that God “knows that we must grow in spiritual cleanliness and stature to be able to live in His presence.”

medium.q: Why did President Eyring tell the story of his father staying by his mother’s side and thanking the nurses?
options: To show that gratitude can take away the pain of loss
To explain how his family came to value medical care
To show that trials end quickly for those with faith
As evidence that the Lord sends disciples to help others
medium.why: He said he told the story as evidence that “the Lord sends faithful disciples to help Him keep His promise to succor others in their distress.”

medium.q: You pray to know whom the Lord would have you help, a name comes to mind, and you reach out. What did President Eyring say this is to that person?
options: A sign that their trial is almost over
Evidence that the Lord knew and loved them
A reminder to ask for help sooner
Proof that you had time to spare
medium.why: He taught, “That you felt prompted to reach out to them was evidence to them that the Lord knew and loved them.”

medium.q: President Eyring quoted Alma’s words about being “willing to mourn with those that mourn.” What opportunity was he describing?
options: Keeping a record of the trials we have overcome
Learning to carry our own burdens without help
Inviting the Holy Ghost to help us find ways to comfort others
Choosing a time to rest from serving others
medium.why: He introduced Alma’s words by saying a great opportunity comes when we invite the Holy Ghost to help us find ways to help the Lord comfort those pleading for it.

hard.q: President Eyring said no two people’s trials are exactly alike. What did he say is the same for every person, at all times?
options: How long the hardest trials will last
The kind of help that brings relief
The season of life when tests come
What is being tested: will we obey the Lord
hard.why: Trials vary, but he said what is being tested is the same: “Will we do whatsoever the Lord our God will command us?”

hard.q: President Eyring’s mother had medical trials all her life, yet he said the Lord’s promise was fulfilled for her. Which statement best explains how both can be true in this talk?
options: The promise is relief from trials, and hers were finally taken away
The promise is His aid and presence in trials, and she trusted it
The promise is for the next life, and she received it only there
The promise is for the untested, and she was spared the worst trials
hard.why: He said “the promise is not for the removal of challenges.” Her trials stayed, but because she knew the Lord’s words were true, “the Lord’s promise was fulfilled for her.”

hard.q: President Eyring taught that the Savior does more than understand our grief. Which statement gives the whole of what he said?
options: He has felt grief and has also borne and carried ours
He has watched our grief with perfect compassion
He has felt grief of His own and so can pity ours
He will understand our grief when we tell Him of it
hard.why: He said the Savior “not only understands and has felt grief,” but has also borne your griefs and carried your sorrows. He knows you perfectly and knows your heart.

hard.q: Which act best fits what President Eyring taught about helping those who serve in Church callings?
options: Offering a new teacher a list of ways to improve
Asking that a tired leader be given a lighter calling
Telling a leader you appreciate her and trust she has been inspired
Saving your thanks for the day a leader is released
hard.why: He taught that as we show appreciation and confidence that those who serve have been inspired, “they will feel evidence that God called them, knows them, and has guided and blessed them.”

hard.q: In his closing testimony, how did President Eyring say the Lord keeps His promises?
options: Through the Holy Spirit and through His faithful disciples
Through taking trials away and through shortening them
Through those with callings and through no one else
Through blessings held back until after this life
hard.why: He testified that the Lord “keeps His promises, both through the Holy Spirit and through His loving, true, faithful disciples.”
